constraint_decided_it: E94's scope note: 'Note that using an instance of E94 Space Primitive for approximating the actual extent of some place always defines a (declarative) instance of E53 Place in its own right' -- the declarative place defined by P168 is a different E53 from the cut's phenomenal extent, and E94 adds that 'Definitions of instances of E53 Place using different spatial reference systems are always definitions of different instances of E53 Place'. A asserts the contrary in terms ('identity of the Place is derived from the geometric definition itself, not approximated from it') while citing t1118, the very thread that put that sentence into the scope note (Doerr's new last paragraph: 'Any geometric approximation of such a place by an instance of E94 Space Primitive constitutes an instance of E53 Place in its own right'; Hiebel: geometries 'are different places ... to the phenomenal ones ... even if the geometries try to approximate a phenomena'). B never makes that identification explicitly and cites SP6 Declarative Place, whose scope note carries the approximation clause.
better_modelling: Three nodes, not one place: (1) the grave cut is an E26 Physical Feature (E18's scope note names holes as features) and P156 occupies an E53 Place -- the phenomenal extent, in the reference space at rest relative to the feature, with fuzzy boundaries; (2) a separate declarative E53 Place P168 place is defined by the E94 Space Primitive 'POLYGON ((...))' in its stated CRS; (3) the declarative place P189 approximates (E53 -> E53) the phenomenal one. P189's own scope note describes exactly this case: survey/GPS coordinates 'do not state the actual place ... but tr[y] to approximate it with a "declarative" place', and if the total station's maximum deviation is known the feature may additionally be bound with P171 at some place within. The answer to the archivist is unchanged -- the geometry is first-class CRM data -- but it hangs off its own E53, not off the cut's.
reasoning: Both answers get the in-scope call and the E53/P168/E94 construct right, and both quote E94 and P171/P172 accurately (P168 domain E53 range E94 checks out, as does P171/P172's 'not precisely known' framing; B's Objectives quote 'not optimised for implementation specific storage and processing factors' is verbatim, and its SP5-is-historical and P157/H.M.S. Victory claims both verify). A is wrong because it collapses the declarative place into the cut's phenomenal extent and explicitly denies the approximation relation that E94's scope note and t1118 make mandatory, so the P189 link is not merely omitted but ruled out. B commits the same conflation only implicitly and omits P189, which is suboptimal rather than wrong; nothing in the archive leaves this open -- t1118 is a decided thread and the resolution is in the current scope note.
